note: Counterfactuals vary ONE user-controlled profile input at a time, re-score through the REAL handler, and re-classify the affected sentence. The semantic-similarity case varies profile content AND a simulated re-embed of that changed content: the substituted vector is the experiment's deterministic stand-in for re-embedding the edited profile — vectors are computed, never user-authored. orgId is NOT varied as a user action (assigned by the organization); the retired probe is recorded separately under simulatorLevelProbes.

cases.note: User replaces their interest tags with an unrelated set; the interest sentence must lose its feature support.
User raises their experience level to the partner's own (gap 0 -> 0.7) via the profile experience field accepted by updateProfile; the ideal-gap sentence must lose support.

User adds a language they speak to their profile (updateProfile accepts languages); the language-compatibility sentence must GAIN support (false_reason -> supported_contribution), showing the audit also catches sentences newly backed by an edit.

User moves their field from technology to design via their profile; industryMatch drops 1.0 -> 0.3 and the composite score must decrease, yet no sentence cites industryMatch (the computed-but-unsurfaced finding), so the emitted explanation set must be unchanged: a silent score change a profile edit can cause.

cases.variedInput: scoringData.profile.interests + scoringData.embedding.vector (derived re-embed of the edited content)
cases.note: User adds 'technology' to their interest tags; the experiment then substitutes a deterministic stand-in vector for the re-embedding of that changed profile content (rotated so similarity drops to 0.8, no longer > 0.8). The substituted vector is DERIVED, not user-authored: users edit content, the embedding model recomputes the vector. The semantic-similarity sentence must lose support.

simulatorLevelProbes.note: Simulator-only receipt: the simulator moves the org identifier to an arbitrary value — an action no user can perform, since that identifier is assigned by the organization. Both the sentence classification AND the composite score must stay unchanged, recording that the identical-constraint short-circuit ignores org identity entirely. Kept out of the user-action list per reviewer feedback.
